result.title: GAIDA: Generative AI for Human-in-the-Loop Document Annotation
result.summary: Document annotation is a fundamental yet labor-intensive step in building document information extraction systems. While Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and Large Language Models (LLMs) can automate parts of this process, we argue that annotation systems should be judged not by how completely they remove human effort, but by how effectively they redirect it toward review and correction. We propose a modular human-in-the-loop architecture that integrates OCR-based extraction, LLM-based semantic pre-annotation, and human validation in a single editable workflow, and present \textbf{GAIDA}, a research prototype serving as its reference implementation. GAIDA supports interchangeable OCR engines, LLM backends, and prompt configurations, and enables stage-specific measurement of annotation effort. In an initial single-annotator, stage-specific study on the FUNSD scanned-form and WildReceipt retail-receipt benchmarks, OCR assistance reduced region-creation and transcription time by up to \textbf{80.9\%}, and reviewing LLM pre-annotations reduced semantic-labeling time by up to \textbf{73.7\%}, despite imperfect pre-annotations of 78.86\% and 86.98\% Micro F1 on FUNSD and WildReceipt, respectively. Finally, we reuse the same implementation, adapting only OCR and prompt configuration, to build and openly release \textbf{AraReceipt}, a manually annotated dataset of 100 Arabic receipt images labeled with 25 key-information classes. The results indicate that imperfect automated outputs provide practical value when presented as editable suggestions under human control.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 GAIDA 这一模块化的人在回路文档标注原型，整合 OCR 抽取、LLM 语义预标注与人工校验，并在 FUNSD、WildReceipt 上以单标注者实验测量各阶段节省的标注时间。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作重心是文档信息抽取的标注流程工程与效率测量，既不涉及 VLM 内部视觉表示、latent 推理状态或生成/停止机制，也未提出可迁移到 LVR 的表示、训练或推理方法线索，故排除。
